                                             SOAH ORDER NO. 35
                 REQUIRING BRIEFING ON REMANDED ISSUE NOS. 11 AND 13 AND
                        DENYING KEVIN KENNEDY’S SEPTEMBER 20 MOTION
         On September 18, 2026, the Public Utility Commission of Texas
(Commission) issued an Order remanding this matter back to the State Office of
Administrative Hearings (SOAH)1 to address two preliminary order issues:



        Preliminary Order Issue 11. Are the proposed transmission facilities
        necessary to meet state or federal reliability standards?


        Preliminary Order Issue 13. What is the estimated congestion cost
        savings for consumers that may result from the proposed transmission
        facilities considering both current and future expected congestion levels
        and the ability of the proposed transmission facilities to reduce those
        congestion levels?


The Administrative Law Judges (ALJs) will not reopen the evidentiary record.2
However, in connection with the issuance of a supplemental or amended proposal
for decision, the ALJs require briefing.


        The ALJs direct the parties3 and Commission staff (Staff) to submit briefing
on Issue Nos. 11 and 13 as follows:
             • Briefs are due by October 7, 2026; and
             • Responses are due by October 19, 2026.




1 Order Remanding Proceeding to SOAH (Sept. 18, 2026).

2 SOAH Order No. 34 Notice to the Parties (Sept. 15, 2026).

3 Applicants’ September 21, 2026 filing, “Applicants’ Directory of Evidence and Preliminary Order Issue Nos. 11

and 13” will be considered an early-filed brief, which may be supplemented as desired by the briefing deadlines
provided.
                                                        2
                                          SOAH Order No. 35,
                            SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349, PUC Docket No. 59475
 Factual assertions must include specific pinpoint citations from the record. While
other parties are permitted to file briefs and responses, Applicants and Staff are
required to do so.


I.      KEVIN KENNEDY’S MOTION

        On September 20, 2026, Intervenor Kevin Kennedy filed a motion for SOAH
to order an independent technical investigation and forensic audit “to ascertain
whether the modeling the Electric Reliability Council of Texas (ERCOT) used in the
Permian Basin Reliability Plan (PBRP) was valid and appropriately constructed.”
SOAH ALJs do not possess self-initiating regulatory or investigative power.4
Accordingly, the Motion is DENIED by the ALJs.

Signed September 22, 2026



_________________________                                    _________________________
Linda Brite                                                  Linda J. Burgess
Presiding Administrative Law Judge                           Presiding Administrative Law Judge

Dee Marlo Chico
Presiding Administrative Law Judge




4 See Tex. Gov’t Code §§ 2003.021, .049. Under the Public Utility Regulatory Act, the Commission has complete

oversight and exclusive jurisdiction over ERCOT. See Tex. Util. Code § 39.151.
